title: Roll back session between retries in Trigger.clean_unused
body:
When the metadata database has a transient disconnect (RDS/Aurora failover, idle-connection drop by the NLB, routine Postgres maintenance), the `UPDATE task_instance` inside `Trigger.clean_unused` raises `DBAPIError`. The `run_with_db_retries()` wrapper is supposed to absorb this, but it only matches `DBAPIError` / `StaleDataError` — and after a `DBAPIError`, the SQLAlchemy session is left in a pending-rollback state. The next retry attempt reuses that invalidated session and raises `PendingRollbackError`, which the retry policy does **not** match. The exception propagates out of `clean_unused`, the triggerer process exits, and every in-flight deferred trigger it was polling has to be reclaimed by another triggerer, losing its asyncio progress.

The project already has the right pattern in `retry_db_transaction` (`airflow/utils/retries.py`), which catches `DBAPIError` / `StaleDataError` inside the retry attempt, calls `session.rollback()`, and re-raises so Tenacity drives the next retry on a clean session. `retry_db_transaction` can't be applied directly because its docstring says it must not be used with `@provide_session` (and `clean_unused` already is), so this PR mirrors the pattern inline.

Validated:
- New regression test `test_clean_unused_rolls_back_session_on_transient_db_error` passes with the fix (`1 passed in 10.20s`) and fails without it (`AssertionError: Expected 'rollback' to have been called once. Called 0 times.`).
- Full `airflow-core/tests/unit/models/test_trigger.py` suite: 49 passed, no regressions.
- `ruff format` + `ruff check` clean.
- `mypy airflow-core/src/airflow/models/trigger.py` run inside Breeze: `Success: no issues found in 1 source file` (host-side mypy prek hook can't set up its venv on this machine due to a glibc mismatch unrelated to the diff).
- Fast prek hooks (`prek run --from-ref main --stage pre-commit`) all pass for the matched files; `mypy-airflow-core` + `mypy-devel-common` skipped locally and verified via Breeze as noted above.

Related: #70961 is an in-review PR that batches `clean_unused`; its restructure to `with create_session(scoped=False)` per retry attempt would incidentally close this issue as a side effect of the rework. This PR is a smaller, targeted fix in case the batching PR takes longer to land.

closes: #74614

+def test_clean_unused_rolls_back_session_on_transient_db_error():
+    """
+    Regression for https://github.com/apache/airflow/issues/74614.
+
+    A transient DB disconnect raises DBAPIError on the UPDATE inside
+    run_with_db_retries(). Without an explicit session rollback between retry
+    attempts, SQLAlchemy's pending-rollback state causes the next attempt to
+    raise PendingRollbackError, which is not matched by the retry policy, so
+    the triggerer process exits. The fix calls session.rollback() before
+    re-raising inside the retry attempt so Tenacity drives the next retry on
+    a clean session.
+    """
+    import tenacity
+    from sqlalchemy.exc import DBAPIError
+
+    mock_session = MagicMock()
+    mock_session.bind.dialect.name = "postgresql"
+    mock_session.execute.side_effect = [
+        DBAPIError("UPDATE task_instance", {}, Exception("connection reset")),
+        MagicMock(),
+        MagicMock(),
+    ]
+
+    fast_retry = tenacity.Retrying(
+        retry=tenacity.retry_if_exception_type((DBAPIError,)),
+        wait=tenacity.wait_none(),
+        stop=tenacity.stop_after_attempt(3),
+        reraise=True,
+    )
+    with patch("airflow.models.trigger.run_with_db_retries", return_value=fast_retry):
+        Trigger.clean_unused(session=mock_session)
+
+    mock_session.rollback.assert_called_once()
+    assert mock_session.execute.call_count >= 2
+
+
